A1.justification: The matching authors, research setup, Theorem 1, Corollaries 1–3, and appendix proofs establish that these describe the same work. Both PDFs support reliable comparison of the main text, mathematical results, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: Figures 1–3 report original simulations of predicted-score distributions and classification accuracy on Gaussian and linear factor mixture data.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and adds Fashion-MNIST data analyses and classification experiments in Appendix B, Figures 4–10.

M1.justification: The ridge-regularized ERM objective, supported losses, and prediction rule remain unchanged. Appendix B evaluates these classifiers on new data; its PCA discussion concerns informative-factor distributions and does not specify a new classifier component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic GMM/LFMM classification only. Appendix B adds real-image classification using Fashion-MNIST classes 4 versus 5 and 3 versus 7, alongside Gaussian surrogates fitted to those classes. This substantially extends the represented data beyond the synthetic setting.

E2.justification: Square, logistic, and square-hinge losses, together with equivalent-GMM-trained classifiers, were already evaluated in v1's Figures 2–3. The original comparisons remain, and Appendix B reuses these methods on Fashion-MNIST without introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: The original synthetic settings remain unchanged. The added experiments adapt the existing accuracy-versus-regularization and Gaussian-surrogate comparisons to n = 512, with standardized image data, PCA diagnostics, and Gaussian controls constructed from empirical class means and covariances.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds case studies connecting PCA-factor distributions in Figures 4–5 to the two universality notions. Figures 7–10 separately examine performance on each training distribution and performance on common Fashion-MNIST test data across Gaussianity and loss scenarios. This supplies substantial mechanism-oriented evidence beyond v1's deliberately constructed synthetic examples.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains its 100-trial averaging and ±1-standard-deviation reporting. Appendix B supplies no additional repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; its new accuracy curves do not establish a changed statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 retain their results, while Figures 4–10 add real-data findings. Figure 6 shows a higher best accuracy for square-hinge than square loss on classes 4/5. Figures 7–10 show larger real/Gaussian-surrogate discrepancies for classes 4/5 and closer agreement for classes 3/7. These are newly reported settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 corrects the one-sided derivative defining the second derivative, and A.2.3 restores the expectation in gamma's square-root expression. Definition 1 also rewords noise independence, omitting v1's explicit independence from y without developing a corresponding model extension. The main fixed-point system, theorem, and corollaries are retained.

C1.justification: The principal claims about asymptotic ERM characterization, universality conditions, and square-loss suboptimality remain. However, v2's conclusion removes v1's explicit claim to be the first analysis characterizing learning performance when Gaussian universality breaks down, narrowing the stated novelty.

C2.justification: New Remark 1 explains how non-Gaussian informative factors affect classifier alignment through nonzero omega coefficients. Appendix B extends the existing higher-moment and loss-choice interpretation to selected Fashion-MNIST class pairs. The underlying explanation and the existing limitations concerning nonsmooth losses and multiclass extensions remain substantially intact.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents standardization, PCA, estimation of Gaussian-surrogate moments using all available samples in each class, and n = 512. These provide limited procedural detail for the added experiments; exact test-split construction and optimizer settings are not specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Ingersoll for Stein's lemma and Xiao et al. for Fashion-MNIST. Section 2 distinguishes LFMM breakdown from elliptical-distribution results, and Appendix B explains why its direct-image experiments differ from Dandi et al.'s conditional-GAN-generated experiments. The broader literature positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The title now specifies linear factor mixtures. There are limited introduction and background edits, a shorter rewritten conclusion, a new explanatory remark, and a new experimental appendix; Appendix A is renamed 'Proofs.' The established main-section and proof organization remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4–10 add multipanel factor histograms, loss comparisons, and real/Gaussian-surrogate accuracy plots, substantially expanding the visual evidence. Figures 1–3 are retained, with Figure 1 relocated, and several overflowing appendix expressions are reformatted. New captions in Figures 7–10 inconsistently name the regularization parameter gamma while their axes use lambda.

improvement.justification: Appendix B adds useful real-image evidence connecting informative-factor distributions, Gaussian-surrogate behavior, and loss choice where v1 offered only synthetic illustrations. Local mathematical corrections and repaired equation layout also help. The gain remains limited: only two class pairs are examined, Gaussianity is assessed qualitatively, and test splits and uncertainty for the new curves are unspecified. The evidence supports improved empirical grounding, but not broad validation on real data.
